theater: 范迪門地東南部與黑線防區

battle.name: 黑色戰爭
battle.theater: 范迪門地東南部與黑線防區
battle.brief: 一八二六年瓦迪門地公司在德文特河谷開埠霍巴特，伐木與牧場伸入東岸，原住民武裝與拓殖隊衝突不斷；一八二八年總督府沿東山脈築起約三百公里「黑線」，二十餘座站所切斷內陸，一八三〇年再以鐵鏈與石牆封死奧伊斯特灣。卡面輪發槍在英軍早於一七四〇年代換成燧發，此時只剩軍械庫舊物與軍官家傳。

kit.name: 輪發槍
kit.history: 最早的後膛手槍。機械太貴，只給火槍隊的軍官與衛兵。

countries: 交戰的兩方，一方是英國在范迪門地殖民地的整套軍事與殖民機器：總督府、不列顛陸軍派駐單位、皇家工程兵與皇家炮兵分隊，以及以囚犯勞役開拓殖民地的瓦迪門地公司；另一方是沒有國家組織的帕拉瓦原住民各部族，沒有常備軍，沒有旗號，靠血緣與地域組成一支支武裝隊伍。英方的指揮分四層：總督府發出追剿令與懸賞，駐軍單位負責會戰，囚犯編成的道路隊與牧場警衛隊守住沿線，原住民嚮導與追蹤者提供情報。瓦迪門地公司自一八二六年在德文特河谷開埠霍巴特起，驅使囚犯伐木、放牧、修路，一個冬天就把東岸與西南大片獵場吃掉，並以自設的「黑線」與鐵鏈把內陸封死。一八二七年抵達的第七十三（高地）步兵營，加上工程兵與炮兵小隊，把殖民地武力提到營級，使政府第一次能連續數月深入內陸作戰。原住民一方分散成多個互不隸屬的小隊，每隊通常數十人，由本地長者或打過硬仗的人率領；部分人靠為海豹獵人與捕鯨船做嚮導、馭獸與採集者維生，因此同時又從海獵船隊手中取得火槍。他們沒有攻佔城市的能力，卻能以小隊襲擊孤立站所、伏擊巡邏隊、切斷車隊與牛群，長期避開與營級部隊的正面交鋒。
countriesEn: The two sides were, on the one hand, the whole military and colonial apparatus of the British settlement in Van Diemen's Land: the governor's office, detachments of the British army, companies of the Royal Engineers and of the Royal Artillery, and the Van Diemen's Land Company, which opened the colony with convict labour. On the other hand stood the Palawa people of the island, organised in kin and country groups, with no standing army and no banners, armed in bands rather than in regiments. British command ran in four layers: the governor's office issued the hunting orders and the rewards, the stationed units fought the pitched actions, road parties and stock guards made up of convicts held the lines, and Aboriginal guides and trackers supplied the intelligence. From 1826, when the Company opened Hobart in the Derwent valley, it drove convicts into felling timber, running stock and building roads; within a single season it had taken a large share of the hunting grounds of the east and the south-west, and it sealed the interior with its own Black Line and its iron chain. The arrival in 1827 of a battalion of the 73rd (Highland) Regiment, together with the engineers and the artillery, raised the colony's force to battalion scale and allowed the government for the first time to campaign deep inland for months at a time. The Aboriginal side was made up of many small bands with no subordination between them, each normally a few dozen strong, led by elders or by men with a record of hard fighting. Some made a living as guides, stockmen and collectors for the sealers and whalers, and so came to hold muskets taken from those sealing crews. They had no capacity to take a city, but they could strike isolated stations with small parties, ambush patrols, cut wagon trains and herds, and they avoided meeting battalion-sized troops in the open for years on end.
people: 這場戰爭的關鍵人物大半不是前線軍人，而是決定政策的人與被捲入政策的原住民首領。總督威廉·索雷爾一八二四至三一年在任，任內把殖民地武力集中到東岸，走的是以剿滅代替談判的路線；一八二四年殖民當局寫給倫敦殖民部與陸軍部的信件中出現「黑色戰爭」一語，最早的使用者是新南威爾斯總督布里斯班，塔斯馬尼亞方面隨後沿用，這個名字自此固定。代理總督喬治·戴維一八二九年出任總督，連發宣告把原住民列為交戰方，懸賞捉拿各部首領，並授權對出現在定居區的武裝分子開火。真正在前線指揮的多是尉官與軍士：一八二七年隨第七十三營登島的各級軍官，負責測量、開路與設站的皇家工程兵小隊，帶著六磅砲進駐霍巴特的皇家炮兵分隊，以及一批被派去守黑線站所的囚犯警衛隊。原住民方面，莫斯基托是東北海岸最有影響的武裝首領，他一度與海豹獵人結盟，後來又為英方遠征隊擔任嚮導，說明兩邊的界線從來不清；金比利、特魯格恩等名字則留在當時的軍事報告、獄方紀錄與後來的口述史裡。一八三二年五月抵任的喬治·阿瑟是全場的轉折點：他關閉黑線、拆毀鐵鏈，把殘餘原住民集中到奧伊斯特灣，改以安置與談判代替出獵。
peopleEn: The key figures in this war were mostly not front-line soldiers but the men who set policy and the Aboriginal leaders drawn into it. Governor William Sorell, in office from 1824 to 1831, concentrated the colony's force on the east coast and followed a line of extermination rather than negotiation. In 1824 the term 'black war' appeared in correspondence from the colonial authorities to the Colonial Office and the War Office in London; the first user was Governor Brisbane of New South Wales, and the usage was taken up in Van Diemen's Land, where the name stuck. Acting Governor George Davey became Governor in 1829 and issued a series of proclamations that placed the Aboriginal people in a state of war, offered rewards for the capture of the leaders of the various groups, and authorised fire on any armed man found in the settled districts. Those actually commanding in the field were mostly captains and non-commissioned officers: the officers of the 73rd battalion that landed with the regiment in 1827, the small Royal Engineers detachment that did the surveying, the road work and the siting of the stations, the Royal Artillery detachment that brought its six-pounder guns into Hobart, and the convict guards detailed to hold the stations of the Black Line. On the Aboriginal side the most influential armed leader on the north-east coast was Musquito, who at one point allied with the sealers and later served as a guide to British expeditions, which shows how blurred the line between the two sides was; the names of King Billy and Trugern survive in military reports, prison records and later oral histories. George Arthur, who arrived in May 1832, was the turning point of the whole affair: he closed the Black Line, took down the chain, concentrated the remaining people at Oyster Bay, and substituted settlement and negotiation for the hunt.
kits: 卡面這件兵器是輪發槍，一五〇〇年前後的西班牙式後膛手槍，靠發條驅動的棘輪帶動燧石撞擊擊砧點火，機械複雜、造價高昂，當年只配給火槍隊的軍官與衛兵。它的血緣一路傳到英軍：一七四〇年代英軍把軍官手槍統一換成燧發，輪發槍自此退出一線，到一八二六年只剩下兩個位置——殖民地的軍械庫裡作為庫存舊物，以及少數軍官手中作為家傳或戰利品紀念。前線的實際配備是另一套：駐島部隊用燧發滑膛步槍，標準是英軍的「褐貝絲」式，約五七七口徑，搭燧發馬鎗，軍官與衛兵配燧發手槍與彎刀；皇家炮兵分隊帶六磅野戰砲，砲台設在霍巴特的海角，那個地名後來就叫「砲台角」；囚犯編成的牧場警衛隊與道路隊同樣領燧發馬鎗、佩彎刀，軍裝由軍方發給。瓦迪門地公司自備的武裝囚犯與雇傭獵手也是同一套火器，火藥與彈藥由海路運來，線路一旦被切斷，站所只剩庫存量可用。原住民方的武器系統則是另一套傳統：炭化硬木矛，矛頭有石製與骨製、帶倒鉤，另有投矛、硬木格擋棍與「塔薩克」投擲棍、石斧或鐵斧；此外由海豹獵人手中換到的火槍在東北部確實出現過，有人拿它打游擊。一八二〇年代末，西部的武裝小隊還學會了騎馬，用從拓殖者手中得來的馬匹與火槍對牧場與牛群作突擊式掠奪。至於卡面那件輪發槍本身：在這場戰爭裡它只會出現在一件事上——作為軍官遺物、軍械庫清冊上的老件，或者軍官從半島戰爭帶回來的收藏；它提醒的正是同一個位置：火槍隊的軍官與衛兵。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card is the wheellock pistol, a Spanish-pattern breech-loading handgun of about 1500 that fires by driving a spring-loaded ratchet wheel to strike a flint against a steel, the mechanism being complex and expensive enough that it was issued only to officers and guards of the musket companies. Its lineage runs on into the British army: in the 1740s the British standard officer's pistol was changed over to the flintlock and the wheellock dropped out of the first line, so that by 1826 only two places remained for it, the stores of the colonial armoury as obsolete stock, and the hands of a few officers as an heirloom or a trophy. The actual equipment on the line was another matter. The stationed troops carried flintlock smoothbore muskets of the standard British Brown Bess pattern, of about .577 calibre, with flintlock carbines, while officers and guards were given flintlock pistols and sabres. The Royal Artillery detachment brought its six-pounder field guns, the battery being set up on a point at Hobart, a place name that has been called Battery Point ever since. Convict stock guards and road parties were likewise issued flintlock carbines and sabres, with clothing supplied from the military. The Company's own armed convicts and hired hunters used the same weapons, and powder and ammunition came in by sea, so that whenever the line was cut a station had nothing but its stores to fall back on. The Aboriginal weapon system was a different tradition altogether: fire-hardened wooden spears with stone or bone heads, barbed at the point, together with throwing spears, hardwood parrying clubs and tussac throwing clubs, and axes with stone or iron heads; muskets bartered from the sealers also did appear in the north-east, and were used on raids. In the late 1820s the bands in the west also took to the horse, and with animals and muskets taken from the settlers they struck at stock and cattle in sudden mounted raids. As for the wheellock itself, in this war it turns up in only one capacity, as an officer's legacy piece, an old item on the armoury inventory, or a curio an officer brought home from the Peninsular War; and it makes exactly the same point the card makes, that the place belonged to the officers and guards of the musket companies.
tactics: 雙方的戰術從來不對稱。原住民小隊的打法是避開開闊地與營級部隊，改在林緣、沼澤、峽谷與山口設伏，用熟悉的地面換取裝備上的懸殊；襲擊目標多是孤立站所、牛群看守點與小股車隊，得手即散，不戀戰、不佔地；夜間用火把與呼喊壯聲威，撤退時往崎嶇山脊與灌叢裡散開，令追兵失去蹤跡；一八二〇年代末西南部的隊伍更開始騎馬接近，用馬匹提速、在狹窄道路設阻。西方的反制則是一套工程加掃蕩：總督府不追求會戰，而是把獵場圍起來。一八二八年起，瓦迪門地公司在東岸山脈上修「黑線」，沿線設二十餘座站所，站與站之間以巡邏連成一道牆；一八三〇年再拉起約四十公里的鐵鏈，橫在奧伊斯特灣與內陸之間，並在「醋山」一線築起石牆與守望所，封死東南通道，把原住民逼向西南。同時，工程兵帶隊、第七十三營分隊與囚犯警衛隊組成掃蕩縱隊，以原住民嚮導帶路、以步槍排封鎖林邊、以馬鎗班追擊潰退者。氣候與地形決定節奏：一八一八至一九年的「大黑夏」火災燒掉東岸大片原始林，也毀了原住民的採集場地，逼他們靠近定居區，衝突因此更密；一八二〇年代後期乾旱少雨，站所給養要靠海路接濟；冬春多雨，沼澤與泥濘讓車隊與追擊隊寸步難行。
tacticsEn: The two sides never fought symmetrically. The Aboriginal bands avoided meeting battalion-sized troops in the open and set up instead on the edge of the scrub, in the swamps, in the gorges and at the passes, using their knowledge of the ground to make up for the inequality of equipment. Their targets were isolated stations, cattle-posts and small wagon trains; they struck and vanished, neither fighting to the end nor trying to hold ground. At night they raised their confidence with torches and shouting, and when they withdrew they dispersed along the broken ridges and into the scrub, taking their tracks out of the pursuers' sight. In the late 1820s the bands in the south-west also began to ride, using horses for speed and to block the narrow roads. The counter on the European side was engineering plus sweep: the government did not seek a decisive battle but set out to fence the hunting grounds in. From 1828 the Van Diemen's Land Company built the Black Line along the eastern ranges, with more than twenty stations along it and patrols linking station to station into a wall. In 1830 some forty kilometres of iron chain were stretched between Oyster Bay and the interior, and on the line of Vinegar Hill a stone wall and a watch post were built to seal the south-eastern approach, pushing the people back towards the south-west. At the same time the engineers, detachments of the 73rd and the convict guards formed sweeping columns, guided by Aboriginal trackers, locking the scrub edge with musket ranks and following the retreat with cavalry carbines. Weather and country set the rhythm: the fires of the Black Summer in 1818 and 1819 burnt a great part of the eastern forest, destroyed the gathering grounds of the Aboriginal people and drove them towards the settled districts, which made the fighting denser; the late 1820s were dry, so station stores had to come in by sea; and the wet winter and spring turned the swamps and mud into a wall that wagons and pursuit columns alike could not pass.
data: 時間線可以拉出骨架。一八二六年，瓦迪門地公司在德文特河谷開埠霍巴特（公司一度稱之為「自由港」），拓殖由東岸轉入腹地；一八二七年，第七十三（高地）步兵營的一支部隊抵島，殖民地第一次有營級常備武力；一八二八年起「黑線」開工，全線約三百公里、設站二十餘座，工程持續到一八三一年；一八三〇年拉起約四十公里的鐵鏈，並在「醋山」築起石牆與守望所；一八三一年黑線駐軍陸續撤回；一八三二年五月阿瑟到任，黑線正式關閉，戰事至此收束，殘餘人群被集中到奧伊斯特灣，一八三三年再遷往弗林德斯島。距離方面，霍巴特到奧伊斯特灣約三十公里，到北岸黑線盡頭的卡波波塔爾要沿沒有車道的山路走兩百公里以上，行軍以單排縱隊穿過灌叢地帶，一日可走二十至三十公里。兵力方面，第七十三營在島上的營力約五百人上下，炮兵只有數門六磅砲，囚犯警衛隊與道路隊以數百計，工役是殖民地人口中最大的一塊。原住民方面，接觸初期的人口估計在數千人上下，官方在十九世紀三十年代初的點算把留在島上的「黑」人記在一千五百到兩千之間，武裝小隊的規模多在數十人，較大的集結也不過百餘。武器數據上，英軍步槍為五七七口徑滑膛燧發槍，六磅砲用罐裝霰彈與圓彈，一八三〇年代尚未全面換用雷管。
dataEn: The chronology can be laid out as a skeleton. In 1826 the Van Diemen's Land Company opened Hobart in the Derwent valley, which the Company itself for a time called Free Port, and settlement moved from the east coast into the interior. In 1827 a body of the 73rd (Highland) Regiment landed on the island, giving the colony regular battalion-scale force for the first time. From 1828 the Black Line went into construction, about three hundred kilometres in all with more than twenty stations, and the work ran on until 1831. In 1830 some forty kilometres of iron chain were put up, and the stone wall and watch post on Vinegar Hill were raised. In 1831 the garrisons of the Black Line were withdrawn one by one. In May 1832 Arthur arrived, the Black Line was formally closed, the fighting came to an end, the remaining people were concentrated at Oyster Bay, and in 1833 they were moved again to Flinders Island. As to distance, Hobart lies about thirty kilometres from Oyster Bay, and Cape Portland at the northern end of the Black Line is more than two hundred kilometres away by a roadless mountain track; columns marched in single file through the scrub at twenty to thirty kilometres a day. As to strength, the 73rd had a battalion of roughly five hundred men on the island, the artillery a few six-pounder guns, the convict stock guards and road parties numbered in the hundreds, and the work gangs were the largest single body of the colony's population. On the Aboriginal side, population at first contact is estimated in the low thousands, and the official counts of the early 1830s put the number of people remaining on the island at between fifteen hundred and two thousand; armed bands commonly numbered a few dozen, and even the largest gatherings ran to little over a hundred. As to weapons, the British musket was a .577 smoothbore flintlock, the six-pounder used canister and round shot, and percussion had not yet been generally adopted in the 1830s.
cause: 要理解一八二六年之後為何會打成這副樣子，須把三條線疊在一起。第一條是土地：接觸時期島上可供狩獵與採集的地面有限，拓殖一旦推進到東岸與西南部，原住民的生計與活動範圍被壓縮，退讓無路，於是衝突由零星偷牲畜變成有組織的抵抗。第二條是產業：海豹與捕鯨業把外來船隊與武裝船員帶進海灣，這些人既販賣武器也販賣私刑，原住民用換來的火槍與馬匹武裝自己，同時又充當嚮導與工人，把自己捲進殖民地的經濟。第三條是政策：殖民當局把每一次偷竊牲畜都當成交戰行為，把每一名出現在定居區的原住民都視為敵兵，一八二九年戴維的宣告把這種邏輯推到頂點，懸賞與開火權同時下放，武裝衝突因此有了合法的藉口。而一八二六年瓦迪門地公司開埠霍巴特、鋪設道路網與牧場，等於把上面三條線的壓力匯到同一個點上。這場戰爭的本質，是一個剛建立起來的體系殖民，試圖用工程（黑線、鐵鏈、石牆）與殘酷的掃蕩，同時解決土地、勞動與治安三個問題；原住民則以分散的小隊游走應對，不求佔領，只求守住獵場與通路。
causeEn: To understand why the war took the shape it did after 1826, three lines have to be laid on top of each other. The first is land: the ground available for hunting and gathering on the island was limited at the time of contact, and once settlement pushed into the east and the south-west the livelihood and range of the Aboriginal people were compressed, with no room to give way, so that incidents of stock theft turned into organised resistance. The second is industry: sealing and whaling brought outside crews and armed hands into the bays, and these men sold both weapons and private violence; the Aboriginal people armed themselves with muskets and horses obtained in that trade, and at the same time worked as guides and labourers, which drew them into the colonial economy. The third is policy: the colonial authorities treated every theft of cattle as an act of war and every Aboriginal person seen in the settled districts as an enemy, and Davey's proclamations of 1829 carried that logic to its conclusion, handing out rewards and the right to fire at the same time, which gave the armed conflict a legal pretext. The opening of Hobart by the Company in 1826, with its roads and its herds, brought the pressure of all three lines to a single point. The substance of the war was therefore a colonial system just coming into being, trying to solve the problems of land, labour and security at once through engineering, in the form of the Black Line, the chain and the stone walls, and through harsh sweeps; and on the other side, small mobile bands that moved rather than fought for territory, holding on to the hunting grounds and the lines of travel.
impact: 這場戰爭留下的首先是地理上的痕跡與制度上的手法。黑線、鐵鏈與「醋山」石牆是殖民地規模最大、最費工期的軍事工程，囚犯在裡面出的力沒有留下名字，工程本身卻長期留在地形上，成為後來地貌學與考古學的固定線索。制度上，總督府摸索出一套現代戰爭式的做法：把人集中到指定地點、用工程封鎖代替會戰、懸賞與獎勵驅動線人、以嚮導追蹤取代正面交鋒；這套做法日後在澳洲大陸的邊境戰爭中被反覆採用與放大。軍隊方面，原住民嚮導與追蹤者被正式編入英方隊伍並記功，這種合作關係此後長期留在澳洲軍旅傳統裡。代價則落在原住民社會：人口由接觸初期的數千降到一八三〇年代的一千五百至兩千人，並在接下來十年再減到兩三百人的群落規模；他們的語言、器物與狩獵場地一起消失。殖民地當局自己也知道手段失當，一八三七年成立調查委員會追查鎮壓過程，雖然結論有限，卻使「黑色戰爭」這個名號在官方檔案裡正式定型，此後澳洲史學便以它作為十九世紀初這個島的定語。
impactEn: What this war left behind was first of all a mark on the land and a set of methods in the institutions. The Black Line, the chain and the wall on Vinegar Hill were the largest and most labour-hungry military works in the colony; the convicts who built them left no names, but the works themselves stayed in the ground for a long time and became fixed reference points for the geographers and archaeologists who came after. Institutionally, the governor's office worked out a modern way of war: concentrating people at designated points, substituting engineering enclosure for pitched battle, driving informants with rewards and honours, and replacing the open fight with guides and trackers; those methods were taken up and amplified afterwards in the frontier wars of the Australian mainland. In the military sphere, Aboriginal guides and trackers were formally taken onto British establishments and given credit for their work, and that working relationship remained in the Australian military tradition for a long time. The cost fell on Aboriginal society: population fell from the low thousands at contact to between fifteen hundred and two thousand in the 1830s, and in the following decade to remnant groups of two or three hundred; their language, their tools and their hunting grounds disappeared together. The colonial authorities themselves came to know that the methods were wrong, and a board of inquiry was appointed in 1837 to look into the course of the suppression; its conclusions were limited, but it fixed the name 'black war' in the official record, and Australian history has used it ever since as the adjective for this island in the early nineteenth century.
result: 以一八三二年五月阿瑟到任為界，這一階段的戰爭結束。道路是這樣走的：一八二八到三一年之間，政府沒有贏得任何一場值得記載的會戰，卻把島的東岸與東南封成一個大監獄；原住民小隊在西南的山地與沼澤裡撐到一八三〇年，然後在飢餓、武器來源被切斷與追蹤網收緊三重壓力下失去攻勢。一八三二年黑線關閉、駐軍撤回，一八三三年殘餘人群被集中並遷往弗林德斯島，一八三六年最後一批被遷到奧伊斯特灣，此後島上只餘數十人。軍事的結果是英方用工程與消耗贏得了原住民抵抗的崩解，卻沒有帶來任何可以稱為戰果的會戰；卡面那件輪發槍正是這個過程的縮影，它所屬的「軍官與衛兵專用」的位置在一八二六年早已被燧發手槍取代，它自己在島上只以舊物與家傳的形式留到戰後，與黑線的石頭一起，成為那段歷史剩下的兩種遺跡。
resultEn: The war of this phase came to an end with Arthur's arrival in May 1832. The road it took ran like this: between 1828 and 1831 the government won no engagement worth the name, and yet it turned the east and south-east of the island into one large prison; the Aboriginal bands held out in the hills and swamps of the south-west until 1830, and then lost the initiative under three pressures at once, hunger, the cutting-off of their supply of weapons, and a closing net of trackers. In 1832 the Black Line was closed and the garrisons withdrawn; in 1833 the remaining people were concentrated and moved to Flinders Island; in 1836 the last batch was moved to Oyster Bay, and after that only a few dozen remained on the island. The military result was that the European side broke Aboriginal resistance by engineering and attrition, without winning any battle that could be called a victory. The wheellock pistol on this card is the emblem of that process: the place it occupied, the officer and the guard of the musket company, had been taken over by the flintlock pistol long before 1826, and on the island the wheellock survived only as old stock and as an heirloom, which, with the stones of the Black Line, are the two kinds of relic left by that piece of history.
